title: K3 surfaces, Picard lattices and symplectic boundedness
summary: Native K3 geometry over every field, geometric and arithmetic Picard lattices, uniform bounds for finite automorphism subgroups, and fixed-degree polarized moduli over the integers.

layers.title: Native surfaces and the K3 predicate

targets.name: AlgebraicGeometry.IsK3
targets.title: One unpolarized predicate
targets.statement: For a field k and f:X→Spec k, define IsK3 f to be SmoothOfRelativeDimension 2 f ∧ IsProper f ∧ GeometricallyIntegral f ∧ Nonempty(det Ω¹_{X/k} ≅ O_X) ∧ H¹(X,O_X)=0. It is a proposition, with no chosen trivialization, polarization or embedding.
hypotheses: X a native Scheme with f:X→Spec k

locator.where: Chapter 1 Definition 1.1, p.7; huybrechts lines 133–146

targets.proofSketch: Use the native module sheaf and its determinant; H¹ is the module cohomology supplied with duality. Smooth dimension 2 makes det Ω¹=∧²Ω¹.

api.name: IsK3.mk
api.statement: The five conditions construct a proof of IsK3.

api.name: IsK3.iff_conditions
api.statement: IsK3 is equivalent to precisely the five displayed conditions.

api.name: IsK3.canonicalIso
api.statement: The smooth dualizing line identifies canonically with det Ω¹; any isomorphism with O is existential.

targets.name: isK3_iso_and_fieldExtension_iff
targets.title: Isomorphisms and arbitrary field extension
targets.statement: For every isomorphism over k the K3 predicate is invariant; for every extension K/k, IsK3(X_K/K) ↔ IsK3(X/k). These equivalences respect identity extensions and towers.

locator.where: Chapter 17 §2.1, p.365; huybrechts lines 13964–13970

targets.proofSketch: Descent and base change handle relative smoothness, properness, dimension and geometric integrality. Flat coherent base change handles H¹ and differentials. For a line bundle on a proper geometrically integral scheme, triviality is equivalent to nonzero global sections of it and its inverse; their nonzero product is a constant, so they trivialize it. Faithfulness detects the two nonzero spaces over k.

tests.name: identity_extension
tests.statement: K=k gives identity transport.

tests.name: inseparable_extension
tests.statement: The equivalence includes purely inseparable extensions.

tests.name: rescale_form
tests.statement: Multiplying a geometric volume form by a nonzero scalar changes no predicate.

targets.name: IsK3.projective
targets.title: Projectivity over the original field
targets.statement: Every K3 surface over an arbitrary field k is projective over k.
hypotheses: k an arbitrary field, including imperfect fields

locator.where: Chapter 1 Remark 1.2, p.7; huybrechts line 147

targets.proofSketch: Apply the general smooth proper surface projectivity theorem required from the scheme owner, with relative smoothness of dimension 2 and geometric integrality supplied by 1.1. The supplier contract retains its full arbitrary-field surface statement and its modification/ample-support proof. Projectivity is not inferred merely from projectivity after algebraic closure.

tests.name: plane_projective
tests.statement: A smooth quartic has O(1) as an ample witness; it satisfies the native predicate rather than carrying an embedding as data.

tests.name: dimension_control
tests.statement: The argument is a surface theorem and does not assert projectivity of all smooth proper varieties.

tests.name: imperfect_control
tests.statement: Relative smoothness is retained over imperfect k; regularity alone is not the stated hypothesis.

targets.name: IsK3.riemannRoch
targets.title: Coherent invariants and contraction
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X/k, ω=∧²Ω¹, h⁰(O)=h²(O)=1, χ(O)=2 and 2χ(L)=4+L² in ℤ for every invertible L. For each nonzero σ∈H⁰(ω), v↦(w↦σ(v,w)) identifies T_X with Ω¹_X; scaling σ scales this map.
hypotheses: L invertible; σ nonzero for contraction

locator.where: Chapter 1 §2.3 equation (2.5), pp.11–12; huybrechts lines 142,305,316

targets.proofSketch: Proper geometric integrality identifies global functions with k; Serre duality gives h². Apply surface RR geometrically and transport Euler characteristics and intersections by base change. A local frame computes contraction.

tests.name: rr_unit
tests.statement: L=O gives 2χ=4, including characteristic 2: division never occurs in k.

tests.name: rr_quartic
tests.statement: For a quartic hyperplane H, H²=4 and χ(H)=4.

tests.name: contraction_frame
tests.statement: If σ(e₁,e₂)=1, e₁ maps to e₂* and e₂ to -e₁*; in characteristic 2 the latter sign becomes plus.

targets.name: IsK3.numericalKernel_eq_zero
targets.title: Numerical and torsion kernels
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X/k, a line-bundle class whose intersection with every class of Pic(X) is zero is trivial. In particular Pic(X) has no nontrivial torsion, in any characteristic.

locator.where: Chapter 1 Proposition 2.4 and Remark 2.5, p.12; huybrechts lines 335–354

targets.proofSketch: Fix a k-ample H. A nontrivial L with L·H=0 has no section, nor does its inverse, since every nonzero effective divisor has positive H-intersection. Duality gives χ(L)≤0; numerical triviality and RR give χ(L)=2. Torsion is numerically trivial by cancellation in integer intersections.

tests.name: torsion_p
tests.statement: The argument also excludes p-torsion in characteristic p.

tests.name: effective_minus_two
tests.statement: A smooth rational curve C has C²=-2 by adjunction and is not numerically trivial.

tests.name: unit_kernel
tests.statement: O belongs to the kernel and is its only element.

targets.name: smoothQuartic_isK3
targets.title: Quartics over every field
targets.statement: For every field k, a smooth quartic hypersurface X⊂P³_k is K3, with H=O_X(1), H²=4 and χ(O_X(t))=2t²+2 for all integers t. The Fermat quartic is smooth exactly when char k≠2.
hypotheses: smoothness of the quartic for its K3 assertion

locator.where: Chapter 1 Example 1.3(i), p.8; huybrechts lines 160–183

targets.proofSketch: The hypersurface and conormal sequences compute H¹ and ω. Smooth geometric connectedness gives integrality. Bézout gives H², then RR gives the polynomial. Fermat partials are 4x_i³.

tests.name: quartic_t0
tests.statement: χ(O)=2 although h⁰(O)=1.

tests.name: fermat_F2
tests.statement: Over F₂ the equation is (Σx_i)⁴=0, a nonreduced thickening.

tests.name: quartic_connectedness_boundary
tests.statement: The ample quartic has positive dimension and is geometrically connected; the smooth ample divisor V(x₀x₁) in ℙ¹ consists of two points, so smoothness and ampleness without positive dimension do not suffice.

layers.examples: Smooth quartics, the empty scheme, P², and products of elliptic curves distinguish the predicate; the quartic polynomial gives χ(O)=2 and χ(O(1))=4.

layers.title: Picard spaces, vanishing and lifting

targets.name: IsK3.relativePicardSpace
targets.title: The relative Picard space
targets.statement: For a smooth proper finitely presented algebraic-space family X→S whose geometric fibres are K3 schemes, represent the fppf sheafification of T↦Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) by a separated algebraic space locally of finite presentation. It is unramified, has trivial fibrewise identity and torsion subfunctors, and commutes with arbitrary base change. Over a field it is an étale group scheme. The unit O_T→(f_T)_*O_(X_T) is an isomorphism for every T→S.
hypotheses: each geometric fibre a native K3 scheme

locator.where: Theorem 3.1.1, Lemma 3.1.2, Proposition 3.1.3, pp.9–11; rizov lines 404,416,440

targets.proofSketch: Prove universal functions by coherent base change from geometric H⁰(O)=k and H¹(O)=0, including arbitrary nonreduced bases. Apply relative Picard representability and separatedness. H¹(O)=0 kills its tangent; 1.5 kills fibrewise torsion. Relative unramifiedness uses finite presentation and fibres, not flatness.

api.name: relativePicardSpace.baseChange
api.statement: Pic_X/S×_S T≅Pic_X_T/T, preserving tensor product and zero.

api.name: relativePicardSpace.ext
api.statement: Two morphisms to the representative are equal when they induce the same sheaf section.

api.name: relativePicardSpace.tangent

api.name: relativePicardSpace.arithmeticPoints
api.statement: Pic(X) maps injectively to Pic_X/k(k), retaining the Brauer obstruction to surjectivity.

api.name: relativePicardSpace.universalFunctions
api.statement: For every T→S, O_T→(f_T)_*O_(X_T) is an isomorphism.

tests.statement: Over algebraically closed k the rational points are Pic(X).

tests.name: picard_zero

targets.name: IsK3.infiniteHeightDifferentialKernel
targets.title: The infinite-height kernel input
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p>0, if its one-dimensional formal Brauer group has infinite height and H⁰(X,T_X)≠0, the map d:H²(X,WO_X)→H²(X,WΩ¹_X) has nonzero kernel. Under the nonzero-vector-field hypothesis X is unirational and its geometric Néron–Severi rank is 22.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed of characteristic p>0
infinite formal Brauer height and nonzero global vector field for the kernel assertion

locator.where: Theorem 1.3 proof, p.172, lang-nygaard lines 93–104; nygaard-vectorfields Lemma 3.3; rudakov-shafarevich-inseparable §2, Theorem 5 and Corollaries 1–2, pp.1216–1217, lines 438–497; shioda-unirational-primary Lemma p.234 and Corollary 2 p.235

targets.proofSketch: Prove the Rudakov–Šafarevič vector-field unirationality reduction and apply the general unirational-surface cycle theorem to get rank 22 as in their Corollary 2, then the kernel assertion with the Witt and formal-Brauer comparisons. For this unirational surface, the general surface input gives H¹_et=H³_et=0 and ρ=b₂; Noether from χ(O)=2 and K=0 gives deg c₂=24, and étale Gauss–Bonnet gives b₂=22. This uses only the earlier coherent invariants and general surface theorems, not §2.4, §3.4 or the later K3 lattice. In 2.2, a nonzero d on global one-forms produces a nonzero vector field by contraction. The dual d on H²(O) is then injective; FdV=d and V-separatedness would make the Witt differential injective, contradicting this target.

api.name: infiniteHeightDifferentialKernel.vectorField_unirational
api.statement: A nonzero global vector field on a geometric K3 surface makes X unirational. (rudakov-shafarevich-inseparable §2, Corollary 1, p.1217, lines 481–486.)

api.name: infiniteHeightDifferentialKernel.vectorField_rank
api.statement: The same hypothesis gives Néron–Severi rank 22. (shioda-unirational-primary Corollary 2, p.235; rudakov-shafarevich-inseparable Corollary 2 proof, p.1217, lines 489–491.)

api.name: infiniteHeightDifferentialKernel.exists_nonzero
api.statement: Under the infinite-height and vector-field hypotheses, some nonzero x∈H²(WO) satisfies dx=0.

tests.name: kernel_nonzero_not_zero
tests.statement: The witness must have x≠0; d(0)=0 alone does not contradict injectivity.

tests.name: kernel_p2
tests.statement: The reduction and V-separatedness argument include characteristic 2 without dividing by 2.

tests.name: kernel_height_branch
tests.statement: Finite height uses Nygaard Corollary 2.7 instead; no unirationality assertion follows merely from infinite height.

targets.name: IsK3.regularOneForms_closed
targets.title: The positive-characteristic closedness theorem
targets.statement: For every K3 surface in characteristic p>0, the differential d:H⁰(X,Ω¹)→H⁰(X,Ω²) is zero.

locator.where: Theorem 1.3, pp.172–173; lang-nygaard lines 76–104

targets.proofSketch: Extend to an algebraic closure, a perfect field. Finite-height formal Brauer gives Hodge–de Rham degeneration by Nygaard Corollary 2.7. In infinite height, Serre duality turns a nonzero differential into injectivity on H²(O); FdV=d then forces any Witt differential kernel into every image of V, contradicting the separate kernel theorem. The kernel and its vector-field/unirationality reduction are the earlier target §2.1a `IsK3.infiniteHeightDifferentialKernel`.

tests.name: closed_char_two
tests.statement: No division by 2 or restriction p>2 occurs.

tests.name: zero_form
tests.statement: The zero one-form is closed.

tests.name: no_automatic_surface_degeneration
tests.statement: No assertion of degeneration for arbitrary surfaces follows from this K3 theorem.

targets.name: IsK3.noVectorFields
targets.title: Vanishing in all characteristics
targets.statement: For every K3 surface over every field, H⁰(X,Ω¹)=H⁰(X,T_X)=H²(X,T_X)=0.

locator.where: Theorem 1.1 and Corollary 1.2, pp.171–172; lang-nygaard lines 54–74; characteristic-zero branch huybrechts Chapter 1 §3.3, p.16, lines 488–493

targets.proofSketch: In positive characteristic, all forms and their Cartier iterates are closed. Oda identifies them as an image of p-torsion Picard Dieudonné data; this is zero by 2.1. Contraction and duality give the tangent vanishings. In characteristic zero spread out to a finitely generated field, embed it into C, use proper GAGA and projective Kähler Hodge symmetry h¹⁰=h⁰¹=0, then descend.

tests.name: abelian_surface_control
tests.statement: An abelian surface has nonzero invariant vector fields and is excluded by H¹(O).

tests.name: identity_tangent
tests.statement: The automorphism functor has zero tangent at the identity.

tests.name: char2_vanishing
tests.statement: The theorem includes p=2.

targets.name: IsK3.hodgeAndCrystallineRanks
targets.title: Hodge numbers and integral crystalline modules
targets.statement: For a K3 surface over any field, h^{p,q}=dim H^q(Ω^p) is 1 at (0,0),(2,0),(0,2),(2,2), 20 at (1,1), and 0 otherwise. In characteristic p>0 over perfect k, Hⁱ_crys(X/W(k)) is free of ranks (1,0,22,0,1), zero outside 0≤i≤4, and the Hodge–de Rham spectral sequence degenerates at E₁.
hypotheses: k perfect for crystalline cohomology over W(k)

locator.where: Proposition 1.1, pp.59–60; deligne-lift lines 29–57; huybrechts line 367

prerequisites: roadmap:CrystallineCohomology CR.2.3, CR.3.2 (Proper smooth crystalline perfectness and reductions (3))
targets.proofSketch: Noether gives c₂=24. RR for Ω¹ gives χ(Ω¹)=-20; §2.3 and coherent duality leave h¹¹=20. The positions in the diamond force all spectral differentials to vanish, giving de Rham dimensions (1,0,22,0,1). For perfect k of characteristic p>0, put W=W(k) and Mⁱ=Hⁱ_crys(X/W). CrystallineCohomology CR.3.2, Proper smooth crystalline perfectness and reductions (3), gives finite generation, vanishing outside [0,4] and derived reduction modulo p; CR.2.3 identifies this reduction with de Rham cohomology. Since W is a DVR with residue k, universal coefficients give 0→Mⁱ/pMⁱ→Hⁱ_dR(X/k)→M^(i+1)[p]→0 for every integer i. At i=3, Nakayama gives M³=0 and the right term gives M⁴[p]=0; at i=4, M⁴/pM⁴ has dimension 1. At i=1, M¹=0 and M²[p]=0; at i=2, M²/pM² has dimension 22. At i=−1, M⁰[p]=0; at i=0, M⁰/pM⁰ has dimension 1. A finite W-module without p-torsion is free, so the integral ranks are (1,0,22,0,1). This is the universal-coefficient argument of Deligne Proposition 1.1, deligne-lift lines 52–57.

tests.name: euler24
tests.statement: The de Rham Euler sum is 1+22+1=24.

tests.name: h11_twenty
tests.statement: χ(Ω¹)=-20, with H⁰=H²=0.

tests.name: hodge_outside
tests.statement: Exterior degree>2 and coherent degree>2 give zero.

tests.name: crystalline_torsion_control
tests.statement: A summand W/p in M² would force a nonzero quotient M²[p] of H¹_dR, contradicting H¹_dR=0; a summand W/p in M⁰ would similarly force H⁻¹_dR≠0. Perfectness alone does not imply torsion-freeness, including at p=2.

targets.name: IsK3.formalDeformation
targets.title: Unpolarized formal deformations
targets.statement: For geometric K3 X/k in characteristic p>0, its marked deformation functor on Artinian local W(k)-algebras with residue k is prorepresented by Spf W(k)[[t₁,…,t₂₀]], up to noncanonical coordinates. In characteristic zero use Artinian local k-algebras and Spf k[[t₁,…,t₂₀]].

locator.where: Corollary 1.2, p.60; deligne-lift line 58; rizov Proposition 4.1.1 line 756

targets.proofSketch: The supplied cotangent/deformation theory has automorphisms H⁰(T)=0, tangent H¹(T) of dimension 20 and obstruction H²(T)=0. Apply its prorepresentability and lifting criterion with the fixed marking.

tests.name: dual_numbers20
tests.statement: First-order marked deformations form a 20-dimensional tangent space.

tests.name: marking_required
tests.statement: The unmarked global moduli groupoid can have finite automorphisms; the formal marked functor is the one prorepresented.

targets.name: IsK3.lineBundleDeformationDivisor
targets.title: Line-bundle deformation loci
targets.statement: For geometric K3 X/k in characteristic p>0 and a nontrivial line-bundle class L, the marked pair deformation functor is a closed formal subfunctor of 2.5 defined by one equation and flat over W(k), of relative dimension 19. If L is ample of square 2d and p∤2d, it is formally smooth. In characteristic zero an ample L gives a formally smooth dimension 19 locus.
hypotheses: L nontrivial; ampleness for smoothness clauses

locator.where: Proposition 1.5 and Theorem 1.6, pp.60–62; deligne-lift lines 78,131; rizov Lemma 4.1.3 line 779

prerequisites: roadmap:CrystallineCohomology CR.2.3, CR.3.2–CR.3.3, CR.3:duality.1, CR.4.7, CR.7.3
targets.proofSketch: H¹(O)=0 gives uniqueness of class extension and H²(O)=k gives one equation. Deligne’s Gauss–Manin/Kodaira–Spencer argument shows this equation is not divisible by p for nontrivial L: crystalline c₁ cannot remain in F² throughout the universal characteristic-p deformation. At p∤2d, c₁²=2d≠0 makes its tangent obstruction functional nonzero, giving smoothness.

tests.name: trivial_line_control
tests.statement: L=O extends everywhere and has dimension 20; nontriviality is essential.

tests.name: bad_degree_control
tests.statement: At p|2d only flatness of the pair locus is asserted.

tests.name: good_degree_dim19
tests.statement: One nonzero linear obstruction cuts the tangent dimension from 20 to 19.

targets.name: IsK3.polarizedLift
targets.title: A polarized characteristic-zero lift
targets.statement: For a K3 surface over algebraically closed k of characteristic p>0 and any ample L, there is a complete DVR R finite over W(k), a smooth proper R-scheme 𝓧, a relatively ample 𝓛, and a marked special-fibre isomorphism (𝓧_k,𝓛_k)≅(X,L).
hypotheses: k algebraically closed of characteristic p>0

locator.where: Corollaries 1.7–1.8, pp.62–63; deligne-lift lines 140–160

targets.proofSketch: Use the flat pair-deformation divisor to find a finite trait in it: a parameter quotient followed by normalization gives R. Algebraize the ample formal line and formal surface by Grothendieck existence; smoothness and ampleness extend from the closed fibre. This is existence of a suitable lift, not liftability along every fixed deformation.

tests.name: p2_lift
tests.statement: R may be ramified, including p=2.

tests.name: not_every_lift
tests.statement: The conclusion supplies a chosen trait; it does not make the pair deformation space smooth at every bad prime.

layers.examples: The positive-power vanishing excludes O; characteristic2 remains in the closed-form and lifting arguments. A trivial line deforms everywhere, so it cannot define a flat dimension19 divisor.

targets.name: ComplexManifold.IsK3Analytic

targets.statement: On the supplied Hausdorff second-countable native complex-manifold carrier, IsK3Analytic M means M is compact, nonempty and connected, of complex dimension 2, with analytically trivial canonical line and H¹(M,O)=0.

locator.where: Chapter 1 Definition 3.1, p.14; huybrechts lines 405–407

targets.proofSketch: Use the supplied analytic sheaf and canonical bundle; this is a predicate on that carrier, with no parallel analytic-space category.

api.name: IsK3Analytic.mk

api.name: IsK3Analytic.iff_conditions

api.name: IsK3Analytic.congr

api.name: IsK3Analytic.canonicalSections

targets.name: IsK3.analytification
targets.title: GAGA and the projective essential image
targets.statement: For algebraic K3 X/C, X_an is an analytic K3, with natural coherent-cohomology, canonical-line and Picard comparisons preserving tensor products, pullbacks and contraction. An analytic K3 is algebraizable as an algebraic K3 exactly when it has a holomorphic closed embedding in some Pⁿ(C).
hypotheses: IsK3Analytic M for the essential-image assertion

locator.where: Chapter 1 Proposition 3.2 and ensuing paragraph, p.14; huybrechts lines 408–429

tests.name: gaga_O
tests.statement: O_X maps to O_X_an and H¹ is zero on both sides.

tests.name: gaga_volume
tests.statement: A rescaled volume form has the same rescaled image.

tests.name: projective_image
tests.statement: An analytic K3 outside the projective locus is outside the algebraic essential image.

targets.name: IsK3.complexIntegralBetti
targets.title: Integral topology of projective complex K3 surfaces
targets.statement: For a projective analytic K3 M, Hⁱ(M,ℤ) is free of ranks (1,0,22,0,1), zero outside degrees 0–4. Its Hodge decomposition has h²⁰=h⁰²=1 and h¹¹=20; c₁:Pic(M)→H²(M,ℤ) is injective, with image ker(H²(ℤ)→H²(O)), and intersection is cup product evaluated on the complex orientation.

locator.where: Chapter 1 §§3.2–3.3, pp.15–17; huybrechts lines 452–511

targets.proofSketch: Hodge symmetry yields H¹(C)=0 and the exponential sequence gives integral H¹=0 and Pic injection. If nx lies in Pic, the map to H²(O), a complex vector space, detects nx=0; Pic has no torsion, eliminating torsion in H². Integral Poincaré duality and universal coefficients then eliminate torsion in H³ and force H³=0. Noether/Gauss–Bonnet gives b₂=22 and Hodge decomposition gives 20.

tests.name: complex_orientation
tests.statement: For a quartic hyperplane c₁(H), its cup square integrates to 4.

tests.name: torsion_control
tests.statement: Rational Betti ranks alone do not discharge integral freeness.

tests.name: exponential_normalization
tests.statement: For exp(2πit), the lifted unit circle t∈[0,1] has increment 1 in the kernel ℤ; the connecting class of O(1) has degree +1 on P¹. Omitting 2πi or reversing the connecting sign would fail this test.

targets.name: IsK3.integralEtaleRanks
targets.title: Integral geometric étale invariants
targets.statement: For every K3 X/k and prime ℓ invertible in k, Hⁱ_et(X_kbar,ℤ_ℓ) is free with ranks (1,0,22,0,1), vanishes outside 0≤i≤4, and its degree 2 cup-trace pairing with the appropriate Tate twists is perfect.
hypotheses: ℓ prime and invertible in k

locator.where: §2.4, pp.7–8; rizov lines 273–300

targets.proofSketch: Over C use target 3.3, then integral singular/étale comparison. In positive characteristic lift by 2.7 and compare compatible ℤ/ℓⁿ systems by smooth proper base change before taking the adic limit. Duality supplies the pairing.

tests.name: ell_equals_char
tests.statement: The assertion excludes ℓ=char k.

tests.name: ell2_allowed
tests.statement: ℓ=2 is included when char k≠2; only the congruence bound later chooses odd ℓ.

tests.name: h0_trace
tests.statement: H⁰=ℤ_ℓ and the trace of the class of a geometric point in H⁴(2) is 1.

layers.examples: The projective quartic agrees on both carriers. A complex two-torus fails H¹(O)=0. Integral cohomology is free, not merely of rational rank22.

layers.title: Picard lattices and arithmetic rank boundedness

targets.name: IsK3.picardBaseChange
targets.title: Picard pullback and arithmetic descent
targets.statement: For K3 X/k and every extension K/k, Pic(X)→Pic(X_K) is injective and preserves intersections, and is bijective when k is algebraically closed. Every geometric line-bundle class descends to a finite extension. A purely inseparable extension of degree pⁿ has Picard cokernel killed by pⁿ. For separable Galois extensions the Picard–Brauer sequence identifies Pic(X)⊗ℚ with the Galois-invariant geometric Picard group tensor ℚ.
hypotheses: separable Galois extension for the last assertion
targets.proofSketch: Injectivity uses nonzero sections of L and L⁻¹. Field base change preserves the Euler-characteristic intersection formula. Over an algebraically closed base the discrete étale Picard scheme makes a spread-out class constant. Descent over finite extensions follows from finite presentation. The pⁿ-power cocycle descends through purely inseparable extensions. Hochschild–Serre and Hilbert 90 give the Brauer obstruction, killed after tensoring ℚ.

tests.name: picard_identity
tests.statement: The identity field extension gives the identity map.

tests.name: closed_extension
tests.statement: C⊂K adds no Picard classes.

tests.name: obstruction_control
tests.statement: An invariant geometric class need not be represented over k; no integral Galois-invariant identification is unconditional.

targets.name: IsK3.picardLattice
targets.title: The geometric lattice realization
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X/k, Pic(X) is free of finite rank ρ and its intersection form realizes a nondegenerate even integral lattice of signature (1,ρ−1) on the image of Pic(X) in Pic(X)⊗ℚ. The quotient to the supplied arithmetic numerical divisor group is an isometry. Over algebraically closed k, Pic=NS as well.

locator.where: Chapter 1 Proposition 2.4, p.12; Chapter 17 §2, p.364; huybrechts lines 335,13945

targets.proofSketch: Over algebraically closed k use 1.5 to identify Pic with Num, whose finiteness and Hodge index are supplied. Over k, inject Pic into geometric Pic to obtain finite freeness; its rational span contains a k-ample positive class, so its orthogonal complement is negative definite. Apply the pinned rational-ambient lattice constructor; the geometry supplies the pairing, not a new abstract carrier.

api.name: picardLattice.carrierEquiv
api.statement: The additive carrier is naturally equivalent to Additive(LineBundleClass X).

targets.statement: There is a universal B, for example |GL₂₂(𝔽₃)|, such that for every K3 X/k some finite separable K/k of degree≤B has ρ(X_K)=ρ_geom(X). locator.where: Chapter 17 Lemma 2.6, p.367; huybrechts lines 14038–14054

targets.proofSketch: By §4.1 each geometric Picard class descends to a finite extension, so its Galois stabilizer is open, also over imperfect k by taking the separable part of that extension. This proves continuity for the discrete Picard group. Intersect the stabilizers of a finite basis from §4.2 to obtain an open kernel, hence finite image. Reduction mod 3 bounds its order in rank≤22; pad lower ranks with identity blocks. The fixed field of the kernel has bounded separable degree. Brauer obstructions are torsion and purely inseparable cokernels are p-primary, so rational descent gives the whole rank. The composite of SchemeAndStackFoundations §§2.10, 2.15 with the inverse of TauCeti.brauerCohomologyEquiv and TauCeti.subsingleton_brauerGroup_of_finite gives H²_fppf(Spec K,G_m)=0 for finite K. This vanishing, or a rational point in characteristic zero, kills the integral obstruction. Descending finitely many generators gives the unconditional unbounded extension.

targets.title: Rank-five genus-one pencils
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X over an algebraically closed field, ρ(X)≥5 implies a surjective genus-one fibration X→ℙ¹ with geometrically integral generic fibre. The fibration is elliptic outside characteristics 2 and 3; in those characteristics the quasi-elliptic alternative is retained.

locator.where: Chapter 11 Proposition 1.3(ii), p.208, huybrechts lines 7879–7888; Chapter 2 §3.3 and Remark 3.13, pp.32–34, lines 1110–1132,1173–1183

targets.proofSketch: Hodge index makes Pic⊗ℚ indefinite. Clear denominators and choose its primitive effective sign by RR. Reflection in effective (−2)-curves yields a primitive nef isotropic class; its complete linear system is a base-point-free genus-one pencil. Retain the possible cuspidal geometric generic fibre in characteristics 2 and 3.

targets.name: IsK3.ellipticSupersingular_rank22
targets.title: Infinite height with a genus-one pencil
targets.statement: For a K3 surface X over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0, infinite formal Brauer height together with an elliptic fibration X→ℙ¹ implies ρ(X)=22; no section is assumed. A quasi-elliptic fibration also implies ρ(X)=22, without a height hypothesis. For every geometric K3 in positive characteristic, ρ≥21 implies ρ=22: finite height is excluded by §6.0a, and at infinite height §§6.0b–6.0c give a pencil and rank 22.
hypotheses: k algebraically closed of characteristic p>0
infinite formal Brauer height and an elliptic fibration for the first assertion; a quasi-elliptic fibration for the second

locator.where: Theorem (1.7)(i), p.547, artin-supersingular lines 192–210; quasi-elliptic alternative huybrechts Chapter 2 Remark 3.13, lines 1182–1183

targets.proofSketch: Apply Artin’s elliptic theorem in its formal-height convention, using the Jacobian-fibration comparison also when the pencil has no section. For a quasi-elliptic pencil over ℙ¹, use the general surface unirationality input and the unirational-surface cycle theorem. These alternatives close the small-characteristic branch without assuming every genus-one pencil is elliptic. For an elliptic K3 pencil without a section, its relatively minimal Jacobian J is K3 and ρ(J)=ρ(X), by Artin Lemma (1.8), artin-supersingular lines 204–210. The genus-one Jacobian construction preserves the fibre-component root lattice (dolgachev-keum lines 493–496); include the quasi-elliptic construction in characteristics 2 and 3 from gap:elliptic-surface-geometry. Its K3 property follows from the genus-one canonical-bundle and Euler-characteristic comparisons in that contract. Apply the preceding rank implication to both X and J whenever their vertical root lattices have rank 20.

targets.name: IsK3.tameSymplecticQuotient
targets.title: Tame quotients and their exceptional lattices
targets.statement: For geometric K3 X/k and finite symplectic G with |G| invertible in k, X/G has rational double points and its minimal resolution Y is K3. The exceptional root lattice R_G⊂Pic(Y) has discriminant prime to char k when char k>0. If char k>0 and rank R_G=20 its determinant is nonsquare. Local stabilizers embed into SL₂(k).

locator.where: Lemmas 3.1–3.2 and proof of Theorem 3.3, pp.10–13; dolgachev-keum lines 399,444,507

targets.proofSketch: Tame linearization makes a local symplectic stabilizer a finite subgroup of SL₂. Resolve its ADE singularities; discrepancy 0 and coherent quotient formulas give canonical triviality and H¹=0 on Y. Use the prime-to-p local discriminants. In rank 20, the exceptional classes and an ample class give ρ(Y)≥21, hence ρ(Y)=22 by §6.0c. Use §6.0 to write |disc Pic(Y)|=p^(2σ). If det R is a square, the rank-two orthogonal complement has negative square determinant and a primitive isotropic vector. RR and reflections as in §6.0b give a genus-one pencil whose vertical root lattice contains an isometric copy M of R with finite index a; thus det M=a²det R(φ). Its Jacobian J is K3 with R(J)=R(φ), so ρ(J)≥21 and §6.0c gives ρ(J)=22. The section and fibre span a unimodular plane; since the Mordell–Weil rank is zero, det R(J)=m²|disc Pic(J)| for the finite Mordell–Weil torsion order m. By §6.0 this is divisible by p, contradicting p∤det R. The Jacobian construction and vertical-lattice comparison retain the quasi-elliptic alternative at p=2,3 (dolgachev-keum lines 465–505). G=1 has Y=X and zero root lattice.

targets.name: IsK3.tameCyclicFixedPointArithmetic
targets.title: Cyclic quotient arithmetic
targets.statement: Let a cyclic group C_n, n>1 invertible in an algebraically closed k, act faithfully and symplectically on a K3 X. For each divisor m>1 of n let a_m count orbits whose stabilizer has order m. Then 24(n−1)=Σ_(m|n,m>1) a_m(n/m)(m²−1), the quotient exceptional lattice is ⊕_(m|n,m>1) A_(m−1)^(a_m) with negative form, and for each d|n, d>1, the order-d subgroup fixes Σ_(d|m|n)(n/m)a_m points. The corresponding relations for every subgroup, orbit divisibility and rank bounds leave n∈{2,3,4,5,6,7,8,11,15}; the last two possibilities are excluded by the rank-20 nonsquare-discriminant theorem in positive characteristic and by the rank-19 bound in characteristic zero.
hypotheses: faithful symplectic C_n action with n>1 invertible in k

locator.where: §5 equation (5.2) and cyclic cases, Russian original pp.108–110, nikulin-symplectic lines 1561–1624; dolgachev-keum Theorem 3.3 proof, lines 511–520

targets.proofSketch: Remove the finitely many points with nontrivial stabilizer. The free degree-n cover multiplies the compact-support Euler characteristic by n, while resolving an A_(m−1) point contributes m to Euler characteristic. Apply the resulting identity also to every subgroup and use nonnegative orbit counts and the root-rank bound. In characteristic zero the projective Picard rank is at most 20, so a negative definite root lattice has rank at most 19. In positive characteristic use 6.1 to exclude the two square-discriminant rank-20 candidates.

targets.name: IsK3.wildFixedLocusAlternatives
targets.title: Wild fixed loci and quotient divisors
targets.statement: For a geometric K3 X in characteristic p>0 and an automorphism g of exact order p, put F=Fix(g)_red. If F has a curve, it is a connected divisor and κ(X,F) is 0, 1 or 2. At κ=0 it is a negative definite ADE nodal cycle. At κ=1 a divisor supported on F gives a genus-one fibration, with the quasi-elliptic possibility only in characteristics 2 and 3 and p≤11. At κ=2 choose a nef big D of minimal multiplicities with support F, set N=D²/2+1 and d=h⁰(O(D−F)); then p(N−d−1)≤2N−2.

The fixed locus is either finite with at most 2 points or a connected divisor of Kodaira dimension 0,1 or 2. In the K3 quotient branch the exceptional locus increases Picard rank, and the rational transcendental cokernel H²_et/(Pic⊗ℚ_ℓ) of its resolution is the g-invariant cokernel of X. In the rational branch H²_et(X,ℚ_ℓ(1))^g is algebraic. In the free Enriques branch dim H²_et(X,ℚ_ℓ)^g=10; this assertion uses the second Betti number, without a Picard-rank identification.

In the rational branch apply the general rational-surface cycle theorem, then the quotient transcendental comparison. In the Enriques branch q:X→Y is a finite étale C₂-torsor, even in characteristic 2. Rational quotient descent gives Hⁱ(Y,ℚ_ℓ)=Hⁱ(X,ℚ_ℓ)^g and H¹(Y)=H³(Y)=0. Since T_X=q* T_Y, the projection formula gives deg c₂(T_X)=2 deg c₂(T_Y). Gauss–Bonnet yields e(Y)=24/2=12 and b₂(Y)=12−2=10.

targets.statement: For a geometric K3 X and a finite tame symplectic group G, write Y for the minimal K3 resolution of X/G. targets.proofSketch: If ρ(Y)<22, §6.0a rules out finite-height rank 21. If Y had rank 21 at infinite height, §6.0b would give a genus-one pencil and §6.0c would force rank 22. Thus the transcendental cokernel has dimension at least two; quotient comparison, an invariant ample class and H⁰,H⁴ give five invariants. If ρ(Y)=22, §6.0a gives infinite height; formal-Brauer pullback and trace, with nonzero tangent, and absence of homomorphisms between finite-height formal groups and the formal additive group transfer infinite height to X. For even |G| apply §6.7d and §6.0c. For odd |G| outside {7,21}, the element-order table and quotient root lattices give ρ(X)≥6 as in Lemma 4.4, so §§6.0b–6.0c apply. The separate order-7 and order-21 character averages each give six invariants. For Artin invariant >1 the nonzero de Rham (1,1) cycle contribution supplies a third H² invariant, or the quotient root-lattice discriminant gives invariant Picard rank >2. Average only in |G| in characteristic p; the crystalline idempotent commutes with reduction and cross-realization transfers its rank to every ℚ_ℓ. In characteristic zero the volume form, its conjugate and an averaged ample class give three H² invariants.

targets.statement: For a strongly projective K3 scheme family over a Noetherian base S and n>0, [n]:Pic_X/S→Pic_X/S is a closed immersion. For a relative Picard section λ the locus of geometric primitivity is open. These statements descend to polarized K3 algebraic-space families after étale localization and extend by approximation.

locator.where: Lemma 3.1.6(i)–(ii), pp.11–12; rizov lines 463–516, with the square-zero case supplied by Hodge index

targets.proofSketch: Torsion-freeness gives monomorphy. On finite-Hilbert-polynomial Picard pieces the valuative extension and intersection constraints make [n] proper, hence closed. For an arbitrary Picard section λ choose an auxiliary relative ample H from strong projectivity. Locally the integers d=λ²/2 and m=λ·H are constant, by the fibre Hilbert polynomials and integer RR. If d≠0, λ=nµ with n>1 forces n²∣d, leaving finitely many n. If d=0 and m≠0 it forces n∣m, again leaving finitely many n. If d=m=0, Hodge index makes λ numerically zero on every geometric fibre, and §1.5 makes λ=0 there; no point on that piece is primitive. In the first two cases the nonprimitive locus is a finite union of the closed root loci λ⁻¹([n]Pic); in the last it is the whole piece. These cases prove openness for every section, including square-zero and nonample sections.

targets.name: PolarizedK3Family

targets.statement: For d>0 and scheme S, a degree 2d polarized K3 family is a smooth proper finitely presented algebraic space X→S with native geometric K3 scheme fibres and a section λ of Pic_X/S that is étale-locally represented by a relatively ample line bundle and has geometric square 2d. Arrows are Cartesian family isomorphisms preserving λ. The primitive subcategory imposes 7.1 fibrewise.

targets.name: k3HilbertLocus

targets.statement: In the universal flat projective Hilbert family of surfaces with polynomial 9dt²+2, d>0, construct a finite-type locally closed subscheme U_K3 carrying exactly the smooth geometrically integral fibres with H¹(O)=0 and trivial canonical class. The construction and its family commute with base change; every embedded K3 with this polynomial factors through it. Use the scheme-theoretic equality locus of the canonical and zero Picard sections, not merely equality of their ranks.

locator.where: Proposition 4.2.1 proof, p.19; rizov lines 831–849

targets.proofSketch: First restrict to the open smooth geometrically integral surface locus, then the open H¹(O)=0 locus by semicontinuity. The general relative Picard representative carries the canonical class and zero section; take their scheme-theoretic equality locus. Its separatedness makes this a closed subscheme of that open locus. Relative smoothness identifies the canonical determinant, and the relative Picard trivial class is represented locally by a line pulled back from the base. This is the required K3 family and is finite type. Over arbitrary bases use the finite-presentation descent and cohomology/base-change comparison to establish the universal family statement.

targets.name: polarizedK3HilbertAtlas

targets.statement: For every d>0 construct a finite-type scheme H_d over ℤ parametrizing linearly normal K3 embeddings into P^(9d+1) of polynomial 9dt²+2 whose hyperplane Picard class is 3λ for an ample section λ of square 2d. It has an open primitive locus H_d^prim and a PGL_(9d+2)-action. Every geometric polarized object is a fibre; every polarized family lies étale-locally in its image after choosing its complete projective frame.

tests.name: frames_not_classes
tests.statement: On the Fermat quartic over ℂ, swapping x₀ and x₁ permutes the independent cubic sections x₀³ and x₁³ and gives distinct projective frames with the same cubic Hilbert point. Its PGL stabilizer is Aut(X,[O_X(1)]), equal to Aut(X,[O_X(3)]) by Picard torsion-freeness. A frame change outside this stabilizer changes the Hilbert point. The frame torsor over a prescribed polarized family also retains its source identification, so these remain distinct torsor points.

tests.name: no_global_root_line

targets.statement: For every d>0 the étale stacks M_2d and F_2d of 7.3 and its primitive subcategory are Deligne–Mumford stacks of finite type over Spec ℤ, with F_2d→M_2d an open immersion. There are quotient presentations [H_d/PGL_(9d+2)]≃M_2d and [H_d^prim/PGL_(9d+2)]≃F_2d.

targets.name: polarizedK3ModuliStack.separated
targets.title: Trait extension, separation and finite inertia
targets.statement: For d>0, any generic-fibre polarized isomorphism between two smooth proper polarized K3 families over a DVR extends uniquely over that DVR. The diagonals of M_2d and F_2d are finite unramified, so the stacks are separated and have finite inertia.

Over the quasi-compact quasi-separated DVR base, properness and relative ampleness give projectivity. A K3 has a nonzero regular two-form; a ruled smooth surface has none, so the special fibre is not geometrically ruled. Apply the general trait-extension theorem and descend uniqueness. The proper quasi-finite Isom diagonal is finite; its tangent is zero.

tests.name: identity_trait

tests.name: not_proper_moduli
tests.statement: The extension theorem extends isomorphisms between given smooth families; it does not extend every punctured-trait family.

targets.name: polarizedK3ModuliStack.coarse

targets.statement: For every d>0, M_2d and F_2d have separated coarse moduli algebraic spaces of finite type over Spec ℤ. The coarse map is universal for maps to algebraic spaces and bijects geometric isomorphism classes with geometric points over algebraically closed fields.

tests.name: d1_open

locator.where: Chapter 17 §3 preceding Proposition 3.8, p.379; huybrechts lines 14545–14548

A k-basis of H⁰(L³) yields a k-point of H_d for every k-isomorphism class, including every twist. The finite-type scheme has finitely many k-points. gaps.title: Projectivity of smooth proper surfaces

gaps.title: Projective hypersurface cohomology
gaps.needs: Supply the projective complete-intersection conormal/Koszul cohomology comparison over every field and geometric connectedness for positive-dimensional complete intersections cut out by an ordered regular sequence of ample effective Cartier divisors in a product of projective spaces.
gaps.detail: Consume SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.5 conormal_regular and §2.20 regular-section Koszul duality for arbitrary regular immersions; these require no positivity or dimension bound. JacobianChallenge Layer C supplies twisting-sheaf cohomology. Connectedness has separate hypotheses: each defining divisor is ample on the product, and the final dimension is at least one. After algebraic closure, the intermediate complete intersections are Cohen–Macaulay and have dimension at least two before each cut. Repeatedly apply SGA 2, Exposé XII Corollary 3.5, p.120 (2005 arXiv v1 re-edition), sga2 lines 4277–4287. Thus the final smooth intersection is geometrically connected and geometrically integral. The quartic in ℙ³ and the (1,1),(2,2) intersection in ℙ²×ℙ² both have dimension two and ample defining divisors. Their conormal calculations are the applications at huybrechts lines 160–166 and 12221–12231.

gaps.needs: Supply Oda’s comparison for smooth proper schemes over perfect fields of characteristic p>0 with a rational point.
gaps.detail: Oda Corollary 5.12 identifies the Dieudonné module of p-torsion Picard data inside H¹_dR, with the appropriate indefinitely closed-form image. Lang–Nygaard Theorem 1.1 extracts 0→H¹(O)→DM(pPic)→H⁰(Ω¹), the last image indefinitely closed forms. State both with conventions reconciled; passing to algebraically closed fields supplies the rational point. The additional comparison belongs to this owner’s Part II.

gaps.title: Arbitrary-field numerical quotient
gaps.needs: Supply the numerical divisor quotient and its functorial intersection comparison over arbitrary fields.
gaps.detail: Main §5.10 specifies the quotient over algebraically closed fields. Extend its definition and compatibility over all fields without assuming that arithmetic numerical equivalence is always geometric numerical equivalence. For K3 surfaces target 1.5 proves the numerical kernel zero directly over k; target 4.2 compares the resulting pairing. Define the arithmetic relation by D≡D′ exactly when (D−D′)·C=0 for every integral k-curve C, using main §5.9 Chow.intersectionNumber, and descend that pairing to its quotient. For a finite field extension K/k, main §5.6 projection_formula gives [K:k](D_K·C′)_K=(D·π_*C′)_k: the right side uses residue-weighted degree. For divisors both pulled back, intersection degree is unchanged by field extension, by flat base change in §5.2 and the normalized degree on Spec K. Over an algebraic closure, every curve and its equations descend to a finite extension; testing with its pushforward proves agreement of the numerical kernels. This proves the required comparison without identifying arithmetic Picard groups with all geometric classes.

gaps.title: Genus-one fibrations
gaps.needs: Supply relatively minimal genus-one fibrations and their Jacobian fibrations over smooth curves over algebraically closed fields, with Kodaira–Néron fibre types in every characteristic, including quasi-elliptic characteristics 2 and 3, including the fibre-component root-lattice quotient and finite-index identity d_M=a²d_R(φ), where a=[R(φ):image(M)] for a maximal negative definite vertical sublattice M, and unirationality of a quasi-elliptic surface over the rational base curve.
gaps.detail: For the general surface statements use Cossec–Dolgachev–Liedtke, Enriques Surfaces I, author draft dated 19 April 2024, Chapter 4. A genus-one fibration f:X→C is a proper morphism from a smooth surface X to a smooth curve C with f_*O_X=O_C, and is relatively minimal; the Euler and global canonical comparisons below take C proper. Theorem 4.1.6, pp.364–366, enriques-one lines 17528–17594, gives R¹f_*O_X=L⊕T and ω_X=f*(ω_C⊗L⁻¹)⊗O_X(Σa_t Fbar_t), where f⁻¹(t)=m_t Fbar_t, deg L=−χ(O_X)−length(T), 0≤a_t<m_t, and a_t=m_t−1 for a tame fibre. Keep T and the wild coefficients at characteristics 2 and 3. For its Jacobian j:J→C, Proposition 4.3.7, p.385, enriques-one lines 18462–18471, gives no multiple fibres, R¹j_*O_J invertible of degree −χ(O_J), and ω_J=j*(ω_C⊗(R¹j_*O_J)⁻¹). Proposition 4.3.14, p.389, enriques-one lines 18646–18657, proves χ(O_X)=χ(O_J) in every characteristic, using the equal torsion kernel and cokernel of the comparison on R¹O. Theorem 4.3.20, p.392, enriques-one lines 18799–18817, preserves the reduced Kodaira fibre type, hence its component root lattice, and identifies nonmultiple fibres. These are general genus-one surface statements, including quasi-elliptic fibrations. The section–fibre span on J has Gram [[−χ(O_J),1],[1,0]] and determinant −1 by Corollary 4.3.8, p.385, enriques-one lines 18466–18471. Its K3 instance is the even hyperbolic plane after replacing the section C₀ by C₀+F. The vertical finite-index identity d_M=a²d_R(φ) remains dolgachev-keum equation (3.1), lines 424–443; for Mordell–Weil rank zero, the discriminant is divided by the square of the torsion order by Enriques Surfaces I, Theorem 4.3.9(3), p.385, enriques-one lines 18472–18483, with the K3 application at dolgachev-keum lines 493–505. Liedtke, Algebraic Surfaces in Positive Characteristic, Theorem 8.3, p.34, liedtke-surfaces lines 1326–1335, supplies the purely inseparable dominant rational map from a ruled surface to any quasi-elliptic surface; over ℙ¹ it proves unirationality. The restriction to characteristics 2 and 3 is its Corollary 4.2 and Definition 4.3, pp.20–21, liedtke-surfaces lines 749–767, with the K3 application at huybrechts Chapter 2 §3.3, lines 1127–1132 and 1182–1183. Curve Jacobians do not supply this surface interface; the K3 p-torsion exclusion is §6.3a and the rank-five pencil construction is §6.0b. For the K3 Jacobian recognition in §6.0c, χ=2 and C=ℙ¹ give R¹j_*O_J=O(−2), hence ω_J=O and H¹(J,O_J)=0 by Leray. No unrestricted equality of the two canonical bundles is asserted.
